title: Existential-Safety-Planning Rubric: Can the FLI D-Grade Be Made Operational and Tested?

original_idea.body:
# Existential-Safety-Planning Rubric: Can the FLI D-Grade Be Made Operational and Tested?

**Problem:** FLI's 2025 AI Safety Index found no company scored above D on existential safety planning, but the criteria for a higher grade are vague. There is no concrete, testable rubric specifying what a B/A-grade plan would contain, nor a check of whether any public commitments meet it.

**Direction:** Derive a concrete checklist (e.g. 10-15 binary criteria) for higher existential-safety-planning grades from published frameworks (FSF, RSPs, International AI Safety Report). Score a sample of publicly available company safety frameworks against it (document analysis, lightweight LLM-assisted extraction) and report which criteria are universally unmet.

**Why it matters:** Turning a fuzzy D-grade into an operational, reproducible rubric gives funders/regulators (Frontier Model Forum, EU AI Act) a concrete target and lets external watchdogs audit commitments. It is a diffuse/fuzzy-reward evaluation needing only public documents - high counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** FLI AI Safety Index 2025 (no company above D on existential safety planning) flagged in subfield context as needing concrete higher-grade criteria. International AI Safety Report 2026 and Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice (arXiv:2602.14457) as criteria sources.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: an operational existential-safety-planning rubric gives regulators a concrete target and enables external watchdog audits.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Derive a checklist + document analysis with light LLM extraction; accessible, mostly analytical.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deriving a defensible rubric + scoring frameworks is somewhat open-ended and normative; deliverable less crisp.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Fuzzy-reward governance evaluation on public docs, labs have little incentive; classic neglected-gold.

low_compute.reasoning: Document analysis + light LLM extraction; CPU/free-tier.

novelty.reasoning: Operationalizing the FLI grade into a testable rubric is partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Index exists; concrete higher-grade rubric is partly open.
